# Notation {#sec-notation}

This page fixes the notation of the whole tutorial. The tables are shared with the other tutorials of the site, so a
symbol means the same thing here as in [Fundamentals of Machine Learning](../../fundamentals-of-machine-learning/index.qmd).
The chapters follow this notation whatever notation their sources use; where a chapter quotes a source's convention,
it says so and names the source. The last section lists what is particular to this tutorial.

The notation consolidates that of the main textbooks: @bishop2024deeplearning [Preface], @deisenroth2020mml [Table of
Symbols], @james2023statistical [Ch. 1], @shalev2014ml [Ch. 1], @theodoridis2025ml [Notation] and @zhao2025rl [Symbols].

## Conventions specific to this tutorial

These symbols are used only in the machine-learning tutorials, or depart from the shared tables for a stated reason.

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal H$ | hypothesis class. This departs from the shared tables, where $\mathcal H$ is a Hilbert space, because $\mathcal H$ is the standard name in learning theory; a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space is written $\mathcal H_k$ |
| $\mathcal A$, $\mathcal C$, $\mathcal X$ | sets are written in calligraphic uppercase |
| $a$, $b$, $\alpha$, $\beta$ | scalars (lowercase) |
| $\hat\theta_{\mathrm{MLE}}$, $\hat\theta_{\mathrm{MAP}}$ | maximum-likelihood and maximum a posteriori estimates |
| $\mathcal L(\mathbf x, \lambda) = f(\mathbf x) - \lambda g(\mathbf x)$ | Lagrangian of the problem of optimising $f$ subject to $g(\mathbf x) = 0$, with Lagrange multiplier $\lambda$ |
| $\operatorname{Bern}(x \mid p)$, $\operatorname{Bin}(k \mid n, p)$ | the Bernoulli and binomial mass functions at $x$ and $k$ |
| $\operatorname{Mult}(\cdot \mid n, p_1, \dots, p_k)$ | multinomial distribution |
| $\varepsilon$ | noise term, $y = f(\mathbf x) + \varepsilon$ |

- **Logarithms:** $\log$ is the natural logarithm, and entropies are in nats; a quantity in bits is written with
  $\log_2$ and says so.
- **Events in Bayes' theorem** are written $A$ and $B$; $H$ is kept for the entropy.
